title: Stroke
description: Set the outline shapes are drawn with — width, colour, dashes — and repaint a selection's outline with the same section.

bubble.title: The Stroke section
bubble.body: The Stroke section sets the outline every shape is drawn with — its width, colour, and dashes. It also repaints the outline of whatever is selected. Both jobs live here.

bubble.title: Watch: draw with a set stroke
bubble.body: Press Watch demo: the program sets a wide, dashed stroke, then draws a rectangle so you can see it.

demo.title: Clearing the selection
demo.body: Escape first, so the settings land on the next shape drawn, not on a selection.

demo.title: Drawing with it
demo.body: Width 10, dashed. Now drawing a rectangle with I — watch its outline.

demo.title: Done
demo.body: The rectangle wears the stroke that was set before it was drawn.

bubble.title: Set the width yourself
bubble.body: The demo's rectangle is still selected. Press Escape to deselect — then set the stroke Width to 12 in the Stroke section.

bubble.title: Set the dash
bubble.body: Set Dash to 8 in the Stroke section. The next shapes you draw will have a dashed outline. (Gap is still 5 from the demo.)

bubble.title: Draw with your stroke
bubble.body: Steer to a corner and press I to start a rectangle.

bubble.title: Finish the rectangle
bubble.body: Steer to the opposite corner and press I again. Your rectangle lands at width 12, dashed by 8.

bubble.title: Repaint the selection
bubble.body: Your rectangle is still selected. Change the stroke Colour in the Stroke section — the selected shape repaints at once. With a selection, this section edits the selection; with none, it sets the next shape's stroke.

bubble.title: One section, two jobs
bubble.body: Set the stroke before you draw, or repaint a selection with it afterwards. The Fill tutorial covers the same two jobs for insides.
